items.title: Herb Morand Interview, 1950-03-12
items.q: We had a combination of white accordion player, Joe Wiggins on alto sax, myself on trumpet, Thomas Till on drums, and Frank Melrose on piano.

ctx.x: Herb, what was your next record recording date after the first Dard session?

Well, I made another record with Paramount. I made St. James and the Farmery and the Wailing Blues. We had a combination of white accordion player, Joe Wiggins on alto sax, myself on trumpet, Thomas Till on drums, and Frank Melrose on piano. And Tom also blew the Frisco whistle. And that record, I loaned it to a friend of mine, and I never did locate that record again. I'm sorry to lose that out of my collection. Of course, maybe I could locate one somewhere. But at that time, they were selling for 35 cents, and…
Herb, were you ever present at any of those famous Chicago recording sessions like the Hot Fives or any of the Oliver sessions? No.
